description: note-publish-live.py's own docstring (and REQ-21) promises: 'ANY of (a)/(b)/(c) failing => refuse, close any open browser session, exit 1, and print the EXACT missing piece on stderr.' The call `ctx, pg = open_editor_ready(cookies, note_key, {...})` (main(), line 184) sits OUTSIDE the surrounding try/finally block (the try starts on the very next line). note_browser_common.open_editor_ready() (lib/note_browser_common.py, lines 44-63) has NO try/except around `launch_context()`, `ctx.add_cookies(cookies)`, or `pg.goto(...)` -- any of which can realistically raise (a cloakbrowser launch failure, a malformed-cookie exception, or a navigation timeout on `pg.goto(..., timeout=45000)`, all ordinary real-world failure modes for browser automation). If any of these raises: (1) the exception propagates uncaught out of main(), producing a raw Python traceback instead of the documented clean refusal message -- REQ-21's 'report the exact blocking reason' is violated; (2) because the exception occurs on the tuple-unpacking assignment itself, `ctx` is never bound in main()'s scope, so the `finally: ctx.close()` block a few lines below is never reached for THIS ctx -- any browser context that launch_context() already created before the exception (e.g. add_cookies or goto failing after a successful launch) is never closed, a real resource leak (an orphaned headless browser process) on a tool designed for real, unattended-adjacent invocation. This directly contradicts the 'close any open browser session' guarantee stated in the tool's own header docstring (lines 35-36).

corroboratingEvidence.note: open_editor_ready has no try/except around launch_context/add_cookies/goto
docstring promise this code path violates on an exception
